title: Karl Storz Endoskope - Wikipedia
content: The company was founded in 1945 and specialises in the production and distribution of medical instruments and devices. It is recognised as a global leader in human medical instruments in the field of minimally invasive surgery and rigid endoscopes used for examining body cavities. After the death of founder Karl Storz in 1996, his daughter, Sybill Storz, took over the company’s management. Karl Storz, a surgical mechanic, founded his company in 1945 in Tuttlingen, initially focusing on the production of instruments and lamps for ear, nose, and throat medicine. In the early 1950s, Karl Storz developed and produced the first endoscopes with a traditional lens system, marking the company's entry into endoscopy. Karl Storz's instruments played a key role in promoting the surgical technique, contributing to the development of the field and expansion of the company. The company also supports the Karl Storz Foundation, established in October 2023 by Sybill and Karl-Christian Storz, which aims to support social and medical projects and is committed to nature and environmental protection.

title: German company brings life to empty warehouse
content: Employees ship hundreds of packages daily from this shipping area at the Karl Storz Endoscopy Co. at the former American Optical facility in Southbridge. While getting acquainted with her new work surroundings at Karl Storz Endoscopy — America Inc., Sharon Duhamel of Charlton knew she had been here before. Since 2000, Ms. Duhamel has worked as a distributor, inspector and picker for the German-based medical device manufacturer, which recently moved its logistics operations into a 47,000 square foot warehouse that American Optical had used when it was in operation. Ms. Duhamel, who had picked and shipped eyeglass frames for AO from 1972 to 1984, pointed to a space about five feet from her new workstation. “I try to look and walk around and see how it was set up, where the break room was,” said Ms. Duhamel, who left AO to have children. Karl Storz wanted to build a center to clean instruments that come in from hospitals, so the company had to do massive plumbing and electrical work, he said.
